title: The mask-restricted subset fold visits two-to-the-masked-count subsets
statement: For any Bool-valued mask P and any width n, the mask-restricted subset sum of the constant summand 1 equals 2 raised to the number of indices below n that the mask holds. Nat.Subsets.sumSubsets_card pins the UNRESTRICTED fold at 2^n; this pins the masked one at two-to-the-masked-count, which is the number of divisors a squarefree number has. It is the only law about the masked fold that a fold ignoring its mask fails -- the split law, the grading law and the vanishing law all hold for that fold, because none of them compares the masked fold against anything that counts.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.Subsets.sumSubsetsOn_card : ((x0 : ((x0 : AxNat) -> Bool)) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (AxNat.Subsets.sumSubsetsOn x0 x1 (fun (x2 : ((x2 : AxNat) -> Bool)) => AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) (AxNat.pow (AxNat.succ (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) (AxNat.countRange x0 x1))))

evidence.supports: Nat.Subsets.sumSubsetsOn_card is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example nat_theorem_inventory -- Nat.Subsets.sumSubsetsOn_card 2>/dev/null | grep -Fc '(AxNat.pow (AxNat.succ (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) (AxNat.countRange x0 x1))')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: The pattern is the right-hand side as rendered by Kernel::render_lean, so a statement whose exponent drifted back to the bare width x1 -- which is exactly what a fold ignoring its mask satisfies -- fails this check. The induction's mask-on branch runs the same x + x = (0 + x) + x = x * 2 = pow 2 (succ c) chain Nat.Subsets.sumSubsets_card runs, with c the masked count instead of the width.

evidence.notes: the_card_law_agrees_with_the_fold_at_a_concrete_mask evaluates both sides at the mask (. = 1) and width 3 and adds the control that the result must NOT be pow 2 3. the_masked_fold_visits_only_the_masked_indices names the same 8 as the value a fold ignoring the mask gives. Magnitudes stay tiny: this prelude's numerals are unary succ towers.

notes: Landed by lane mobius-transfer (ADR-1671). ADR-1658 left open whether to restrict the enumeration or to enumerate the support into [0,k); this fact is the restricted enumeration's correctness statement. It does not yet transfer to divisors -- the range-to-subset sum transfer (ADR-1658's missing piece B) is unchanged -- but it does establish that the two sides now have the same CARDINALITY, which before was false by a factor of 2^(bound m - omega(n)).
